method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: TNF and IL-17 inhibitors in axSpA: secukinumab, ixekizumab, comparative efficacy
topic.coverageNote: Comparative statements are the review's own summary, not a head-to-head trial. Trial percentages are those the review reports.

mcqs.question: How does this review position TNF inhibitors and IL-17 inhibitors for axial disease?

options.A: TNF inhibitors are a well-established first-line biologic; IL-17 inhibitors provide comparable efficacy for axial disease
options.B: IL-17 inhibitors replace TNF inhibitors because TNF inhibitors have no axial efficacy
options.C: Neither class is effective for axial disease
options.D: TNF inhibitors are used only for psoriasis and never for the spine
options.E: IL-17 inhibitors are contraindicated in ankylosing spondylitis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: TNF inhibitors are a well-established first-line biologic; IL-17 inhibitors provide comparable efficacy for axial disease
mcqs.explanation: TNF inhibitors remain a well-established first-line biologic. IL-17 inhibitors provide comparable efficacy for axial disease and are particularly advantageous when psoriasis is significant or tuberculosis risk is increased.

sourceRefs.excerpt: TNF inhibitors remain a well-established first-line biologic option with extensive long-term data and proven efficacy for extra-articular manifestations such as uveitis and IBD. Similarly, IL-17 inhibitors provide comparable efficacy for axial disease

mcqs.question: Which extra-articular manifestations does the review specifically attach to the long-term efficacy of TNF inhibitors?

options.E: None; the review says TNF inhibitors worsen uveitis

mcqs.explanation: The review cites proven TNF-inhibitor efficacy for extra-articular manifestations such as uveitis and IBD.

sourceRefs.excerpt: proven efficacy for extra-articular manifestations such as uveitis and IBD

mcqs.question: What week-16 ASAS20 result does the review give for secukinumab in MEASURE 1 and 2?

options.A: Approximately 60–61% with secukinumab 150 mg and 75 mg versus 29% with placebo
options.B: Approximately 10% with secukinumab versus 80% with placebo

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Approximately 60–61% with secukinumab 150 mg and 75 mg versus 29% with placebo
mcqs.explanation: In MEASURE 1 and 2, ASAS20 at week 16 was approximately 60–61% with secukinumab 150 mg and 75 mg versus 29% with placebo. ASAS40 was approximately 28–36% versus 11%.

sourceRefs.excerpt: ASAS20 response at week 16 was approximately 60%–61% with secukinumab 150 mg and 75 mg compared with 29% with placebo

mcqs.question: What did COAST-X show for ixekizumab in non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, as summarized here?

options.A: ASAS40 of 35–40% at week 16 with 80 mg every 2 or 4 weeks, versus 19% with placebo
options.B: No difference from placebo at week 16
options.C: Ixekizumab is approved only for rheumatoid arthritis
options.E: The trial used a 10 mg dose

mcqs.correctAnswerText: ASAS40 of 35–40% at week 16 with 80 mg every 2 or 4 weeks, versus 19% with placebo
mcqs.explanation: Ixekizumab 80 mg every 4 weeks or every 2 weeks yielded ASAS40 rates of 35–40% at week 16 versus 19% on placebo, and the review links this to approval for active non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis with objective inflammation.

sourceRefs.excerpt: ixekizumab 80 mg every 4 weeks or every 2 weeks yielded ASAS40 response rates of 35%–40% at week 16 compared with 19% on placebo

mcqs.question: Which drug does the review identify as the first IL-17A inhibitor approved for ankylosing spondylitis?
mcqs.explanation: The MEASURE trials established secukinumab as the first IL-17A inhibitor approved for ankylosing spondylitis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The MEASURE trials established secukinumab as the first IL-17A inhibitor approved for AS
